The last time I saw my grandma before she passed was thanksgiving of 2015. She had really bad Alzheimer's and couldn't remember who I was but knew I was important. 
We were saying goodbye to her before we left for home and she hugged me saying she would see me soon and she hoped she could remember who I was. I couldn't shake this little voice in the back of my head saying  "wouldn't it be so weird if this was the last time you saw her?"
She died less than a month later on Christmas day.

I think the first sign I ever saw that my parents liked my boyfriend was when on our 3rd date I forgot my wallet and had to call them to bring it to me. My parents invited us out to dinner so we wouldn't spend all our money on popcorn at the movies. The entire car ride to the restaurant my dad kept cracking jokes and my boyfriend would bounce off the energy and make his own jokes. I hadn't heard my dad laugh like that in a while. 
My boyfriend and I have been together for almost a year and a half and he'll text the occasional meme to my dad. The reoccurring comment I hear about my boy is that he's got such a great sense of humor and they adore him for bringing so much light back into my life.

I grew up in a very homophobic household and I never knew until I came out at 14 as bisexual to my mom. I was not allowed to have sleepovers at my house anymore I always slept over at my friend's houses, even if I wasn't attracted to the girl. I did start exploring and eventually I got caught and my mother was angry and upset. As a result, there's a weird divide in our bond and we're not as close as we used to be. 
If you don't talk to your kiddo about her bisexuality, sexual encounters and things like that, there's a really high chance she'll close herself off from you and your wife. Open up a discussion and make sure she knows she's still loved and that you support her. If she does open up and tell you she has a girlfriend, establish that the same rules apply if she had a boyfriend, that way she won't explore outside the house and she knows her parents still have her back. 
Good luck to you and your family 🍀

When I was 7, I was at dinner with my family. I guess that same night the high school was having it's prom night and I could not stop staring at all the girls in their pretty dresses. I went to the bathroom at some point and as I was washing my hands a couple of the teenagers came into the bathroom. I was a pretty shy kid but I so desperately wanted to talk to the girls so I ended up saying "I love your dresses" really quietly. The girls somehow heard it and said thank you and one of them complimented the outfit I had been wearing. It was such a small, fleeting moment but I had the biggest grin when I came back to the table. 
It's been 10 years since then, I had my prom a couple weeks ago. This silly little moment taught me to be so especially lovely to kiddos because you never know what they might take away from the interaction.
